title: Article 51 of the UN Charter reserves individual and collective self-defence if an armed attack occurs
summary: UN Charter Article 51 reserves self-defence if an armed attack occurs, until the Security Council acts.
body: Article 51 says nothing in the Charter shall impair the inherent right of individual or collective self-defence if an armed attack occurs against a member, until the Security Council has taken the necessary measures. The article is a limit and a reservation. It is not a general permission to use force. The wording on the page includes: "solution of those problems. Article 51 Nothing in the present Charter shall impair the inherent right of individual or collective self-defence if an armed attack occurs against a Member of the United Nations, until the Security Council has taken measures necessary to maintain international peace and security. Measures taken by Members in the exercise of this right of self-defence shall be immediately reported to the".
